model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary shareholders less CET1 retention, net debt zero, per ordinary share, GBP flows bridged to a GBp quote

equity_bridge.item: CET1 surplus above the c.13.0% target at 30 Jun 2026, net of the Curve deduction
equity_bridge.note: CET1 13.6% at 30 June (H1-2026 :1617) less the 7bp pro forma deduction for the Curve acquisition completed May 2026 (:1675) = 13.53%, vs the Board's c.13.0% target: 0.53% x GBP 241.8bn RWA = GBP 1.28bn. The 13.6% is after the interim dividend accrual (foreseeable dividend 61bp, :1673) and after the H1-26 buyback executed to 30 June. The GBP 1.0bn H2-26 buyback announced with the interim results is funded from this surplus, and its shares are not deducted from the share count, so the surplus is credited in full. Guidance: 'pay down to a CET1 ratio of c.13.0%' (:234).

Not quantified in the filings. Lloyds' mortgage RWA floors were largely front-loaded in the 1 Jan 2022 changes, so the step-up is assumed modest: about GBP 4bn RWA x 13% = c.GBP 0.5bn of one-off retention. Same estimate as the LYG build.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (total income FY2020-FY2025, 15,126 to 19,422). The 3-year figure (2.2%) is depressed by the FY2024 dip, when deposit-margin compression offset the structural-hedge reinvestment. TTM income to Jun-26 is +13% y/y on H1, and FY26 guidance (underlying NII >GBP 14.9bn, about +7%) implies 5-6% near-term growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3% 3yr, -0.6% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from the revenue CAGRs (2.2% / 5.1%) and the 5-year EPS CAGR (41.9%). Lloyds distributes almost all capital generation: about GBP 7.3bn of buybacks FY2022-H1-26 cut diluted shares by about 17%, and AT1 was redeemed. Total equity is therefore flat by design and is not a growth proxy. The 5-year EPS and attributable-profit CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID-impairment trough (EPS 1.2p) and are meaningless. The 3-year attributable-profit CAGR (-5.8%) is distorted by the FY2025 GBP 800m motor-finance charge; normalised FY2025 (statutory PAT ex-motor GBP 5,428m, about GBP 4,870m to ordinary shareholders) gives about -1.0%.
historical_growth.notes: 'FCF' here is the bank owner-flow proxy: profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (SBC is already a P&L expense). Reported FCF/OCF is not meaningful for a bank. No SBC-adjusted divergence exists, because SBC is about 1% of income. EPS is diluted, in GBP per ordinary share (CSV eps column); the GBp quote is not used in any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Lloyds delivers its 2026 guidance (RoTE >16%, cost:income <50%, >200bps capital generation) and holds RoTE in the mid-teens rather than the c.20% it targets for 2030. The structural hedge keeps compounding NII through 2028 while impairment normalises from very low levels. CET1 is paid down to c.13% and distributions run at about 90%+ of earnings via a progressive dividend plus half-yearly buybacks. Income growth fades to UK nominal GDP after the hedge tailwind is spent. Motor finance costs nothing beyond the existing provision.
scenario_narratives.bull: A higher-for-longer UK rate curve and the hedge roll lift NII beyond guidance. Capital-lite growth in wealth, insurance and Lex/Tusker adds about GBP 2bn of income, and digital cost-out drives cost:income below 45% as the 2027-30 plan promises. RoTE settles at 18%+, and the shares re-rate further on a pure UK-retail bank with distributions running at about 8-9% of market cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: A UK downturn arrives with faster rate cuts. Mortgage and unsecured credit losses rise to about 60bps, deposit margins compress, and the FCA motor redress scheme is upheld at a cost above the provision. Income falls 3% in year 2, buybacks pause for two years to rebuild CET1, and RoTE settles around 12-13%. That is barely above the cost of equity, which at about 1.8x reported TNAV leaves a long way to fall.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth what it can pay ordinary shareholders after funding the capital its growth requires. The flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (after AT1 coupons and NCI) less the CET1 retention that holds the ratio at the c.13% target, discounted at a GBP cost of equity of 10%. Deposits are funding, not debt, so nothing is deducted for net debt. Value is therefore TNAV plus the PV of returns above the cost of equity. At a through-cycle RoTE of about 15%, Lloyds earns a 5pt spread, which justifies roughly 1.6-1.8x TNAV. The shares trade at about 1.8x reported TNAV (57.0p at 30 June 2026), which already prices in RoTE of about 16%+ being sustained; the probability-weighted value sits within a few percent of the price, so this is a fair-value holding whose return is the distribution yield plus mid-single-digit growth, not a re-rating. The LSE quote is in pence and the flows are in pounds, so a GBp holder carries no FX leg; the LYG ADR holder does.
key_risks_to_valuation: Motor-finance commission redress: the GBP 1.95bn cumulative provision is management's best estimate. The FCA scheme (PS26/3) is under four Upper Tribunal challenges, partially suspended since 2 July 2026 with a hearing not before Dec 2026, and Lloyds (Black Horse) is the largest UK motor lender. Overruns sit in the bear path only.
UK rate cycle: the structural hedge smooths but does not remove NII sensitivity. Faster BoE cuts plus deposit competition compress margins; the plan assumes a 3.50% terminal base rate.
Credit: the base assumes impairment normalising to about 30bps. A UK recession at about 60bps for a year costs about GBP 2bn pre-tax.
Valuation already rich at about 1.8x TNAV: most of the value is the spread over CoE, so a 2pt lower terminal RoTE removes about 15-20% of IV.
Basel 3.1 (from 1 Jan 2027): not quantified in the filings. A modest GBP 0.5bn deduction is taken in the bridge.
UK bank tax and surcharge policy risk, and the gap between the base case (mid-teens RoTE) and management's 2028 >18% / 2030 c.20% targets, which the market may be pricing.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close, GBp); 52-week range 81.82-117.9p. GBPUSD=X and LYG from the same API for the dual-listing parity check only.
data_sources.financials: LLOY.L_Metrics.csv / core_metrics FY2015-H1 FY2026 (annual reports FY2017-FY2025, Q1-2026 IMS, H1-2026 half-year results, all UK filings). H1-2026 Half-Year Results (LLOY.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt): three-half income statement (H1-26, H1-25, H2-25), balance sheet, CET1 13.6% / RWA GBP 241.8bn, CET1 target c.13.0%, ordinary shareholders' equity GBP 41,461m, goodwill and intangibles GBP 8,732m, shares in issue 58,081m, diluted weighted 59,234m, interim dividend 1.58p = GBP 918m, GBP 1.0bn further buyback, motor-finance status (note at :7711-7759). FY2025 Annual Report (LLOY.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:408-416, 1399-1409): 2026 guidance and the GBP 800m motor charge.
data_sources.qualitative: FY2025 annual report strategy section and H1-2026 results: 2026 guidance of underlying NII >GBP 14.9bn, cost:income <50% (opex <GBP 9.9bn), AQR c.25bps, RoTE >16%, capital generation >200bps, CET1 paid down to c.13.0%; 2027-30 guidance of mid-single-digit net income CAGR, cost:income <45% in 2030, RoTE >18% in 2028 and c.20% in 2030. No LLOY.L_Analysis.json existed at build time (being written in parallel); LYG_Analysis.json (same equity) was not read, so the scenario axes come from the filings and the LYG Drivers precedent.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ordinary shares, millions, at 30 June 2026: 58,081m ordinary shares in issue excluding own shares (LLOY.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:609) plus 730m dilutive awards (diluted weighted average 59,234m less basic 58,504m, :7888 and :674) = 58,811m. Per-share values are per ordinary 10p share and match the LSE quote in pence. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are value-neutral at IV. The remainder of the 2025 GBP 1.75bn programme (about GBP 0.57bn after 30 June; H1-26 repurchases were GBP 1,176m) and the new GBP 1.0bn programme (to 27 Jan 2027, :7935) are not deducted from the count; the CET1 surplus that funds them is credited in equity_bridge instead.
inputs.sbc_source: Group equity-settled share-based payments (KPI StockBasedCompEquitySettled): FY2025 211, H1-25 102, H1-26 115, so TTM to Jun-26 = 211 - 102 + 115 = 224. No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed; awards are satisfied from shares, not net-settled for cash. SBC nets out of the bank flow because 'ebitda' adds it back and sbc_pct removes it; it only moves the street basis. reported_fcf = TTM profit attributable to ordinary shareholders 4,758 + SBC 224.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases GBP 1,710m plus ordinary dividends GBP 2,000m (KPIs ShareRepurchases, DividendsPaid). H1-26: GBP 1,176m of buybacks and GBP 1,420m of dividends paid. Interim dividend 1.58p (+30%, GBP 918m), and a further buyback of up to GBP 1.0bn to complete by 27 Jan 2027 (H1-2026 :220, :774). Diluted weighted shares fell from 71,256m (FY2020) to 59,234m (H1-26).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are GBP millions; the LSE quote is pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 GBP = 100 GBp, a fixed denomination bridge, not a market rate. The engine multiplies every GBP per-ordinary-share figure by it, so canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in GBp and comparable to current_price; *_gbp siblings hold the model-currency figures. Parity check against the NYSE ADR (1 ADS = 4 ordinary shares), 2026-10-09 closes: LLOY.L at inputs.price_as_of x 4 / 100 x GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09T21:29Z) = US$5.38 per ADS-equivalent vs LYG ADS close US$5.41 (2026-10-09T20:00Z), 0.6% apart; the 4:1 ratio and the pence bridge hold. The LYG valuation of the same equity (2026-10-04) carried the USD/GBP leg; this build has none, so a GBp holder carries no FX translation risk.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:38:40Z regular close (LSE closing auction; Yahoo Finance chart API). Not an after-hours print.
inputs.tnav_note: Reported tangible net assets per share 57.0p at 30 June 2026, in line with 31 Dec 2025 (H1-2026 :217, :357). Derived 32,729 / 58,081 = 56.35p; the difference is the Group's own TNAV definition. The price-to-TNAV commentary uses the reported 57.0p.
inputs.anchor_sources: H1-2026 half-year results (LLOY.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt): CET1 13.6% :1617, RWA 241,783 :2835, CET1 capital 32,861 :2799, ordinary shareholders' equity 41,461 :4739, other equity instruments (AT1) 5,551 :4742, NCI 225 :4747, goodwill and intangibles 8,732 :4673, AT1 distributions 229 (H1-26) / 245 (H1-25) / 218 (H2-25) :5147, tax relief on AT1 coupons 57 :6229, NCI profit 58 / 25 / 73 :4501, attributable profit 2,836 / 2,274 / 1,922 :7866, diluted weighted shares 59,234m :7888, shares in issue ex own 58,081m :609, pro forma CET1 13.1% after dividend accrual, H1 buyback and Curve :213, motor finance :7711-7759.
inputs.cross_listing_precedent: LYG (NYSE ADR of the same equity) was valued 2026-10-04 on this model: weighted IV US$5.57 per ADS at GBPUSD 1.324 = 105.2p per ordinary share. The driver paths here are adopted from that build unchanged (same company, same H1-2026 filing, six days apart, no new evidence). Anchors differ only in the fully diluted count (58,811m from the filing's shares-in-issue line, vs 58,831m derived from dividend cash) and the CET1 surplus (netted for the 7bp Curve deduction). Any difference in the GBp result beyond those two items would be an error.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP cost of equity of 10.0%, built in the currency of the flows. The 10-year gilt is about 4.6%, plus a beta of about 1.1 x 5.0% UK ERP = 10.1%, rounded to 10.0%. Below BCS (11.0%, about 48% investment bank) and HSBC/HSBA.L (10.5%, Asia/EM exposure): Lloyds is a domestic UK retail and commercial bank with a mortgage-heavy book, a structural hedge, and no material trading book. Same rate as the LYG valuation of this equity. One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not in a per-scenario premium. The motor-finance redress tail is a scenario risk (bear path), not a cost-of-equity premium, so it is charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable. The bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs, including occupancy and operating-lease depreciation (statutory total income is gross of the Lex/Tusker operating-lease depreciation charged in operating expenses). No separate lease adjustment; lease liabilities (about GBP 1.1bn) are not debt in this model.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. AT1 coupons (GBP 447m TTM: H2-25 218 + H1-26 229) are tax-deductible, with the relief booked in tax ('Tax relief on coupons on other equity instruments', H1-2026 :6229), so they come out GROSS pre-tax. NCI (GBP 131m TTM) is grossed up at about 28% to GBP 182m. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI/(1-t), so the flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders. AT1 par (GBP 5,551m) is therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (BCS/USB/WFC/HSBA.L convention).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, with net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; the house precedent for large banks (BCS, HSBC, HSBA.L, NAB.AX, USB, WFC, and LYG for this same equity) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route. That is the same economics (value = TNAV + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and it keeps LLOY.L comparable to LYG, BCS and HSBA.L. Deposits (GBP 500.9bn) are operating funding, not debt. Debt securities in issue (GBP 90.9bn) and subordinated liabilities (GBP 9.2bn) are wholesale funding and MREL, not enterprise debt, so the CSV's total_debt of 100,088 is deliberately not used. OCF is meaningless for a bank (the CSV swings from -11.1bn to +27.2bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = statutory 'Total income' (net of insurance finance expense, IFRS 17 basis). TTM H2-25 + H1-26 = (19,422 - 9,386) + 10,626 = 20,662. 'ebitda' = PBT 7,450 + SBC 224 - AT1 447 - NCI grossed 182 = 7,045 (34.1%). Excluding the GBP 800m motor-finance charge in H2-25 opex it is 7,845 (38.0%). sbc_pct removes SBC, and D&A is 0 (inside operating costs). Cash tax: UK 25% corporation tax plus the 3% bank surcharge; TTM 2,114 / (7,450 - 447) = 30.2%, inflated by the partly non-deductible motor provision; H1-26 1,170 / 4,064 = 28.8%. 'capex' = CET1 retention that holds CET1 at the c.13.0% Board target (which includes a management buffer). Target CET1 = 13.0% x 241.8bn = 31.4bn, so CET1/revenue = 1.521 and capex% = 152.1 x g/(1+g). FY0 check: (7,045 - 224) x (1 - 30.2%) = 4,761, vs reported TTM attributable profit of 4,758. The motor-finance charge is treated as non-recurring: the year-1 margin is set from H1-26 and FY26 guidance, not from TTM. The residual risk (provision about GBP 1.95bn cumulative; FCA scheme partially suspended by the Upper Tribunal, hearing Dec 2026 or H2 Feb 2027, H1-2026 :7719-7730) sits in the bear path. No LLOY.L_Analysis.json existed at build time; the qualitative axes are taken from the FY2025 annual report and the H1-2026 results.

bear.margin_rationale: The BoE cuts faster into a UK slowdown, compressing deposit margins, and unemployment overshoots the plan's 5.5% peak; the H1-26 macro overlay already shows a higher unemployment peak and softer house prices. Impairment reaches about 60bps in year 2 (about GBP 2bn above base). The FCA motor-finance scheme survives the Upper Tribunal challenge with costs above the GBP 1.95bn provision (about GBP 1bn extra in year 2). A bank-tax or surcharge increase is a further risk. Margin troughs at 28% and recovers to 33.5%. Terminal RoTE is about 12-13%, a thin spread over CoE. Retention is held at 0 in years 2-3 rather than negative (buybacks pause, CET1 is not released).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) is +6%. H1-26 statutory income was +13% y/y and NII +10% as the structural hedge reprices; FY26 guidance is underlying NII >GBP 14.9bn and 2027-30 guidance is a mid-single-digit net income CAGR (H1-2026 :525). Hedge reinvestment tailwinds persist into 2027-28, then growth fades to 2.5% GBP nominal by year 8.
base.margin_rationale: H1-26 'ebitda' margin (PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI) was 38.6%, with impairment at an elevated GBP 616m (macro overlay). Year 1 at 38% is consistent with FY26 guidance: cost:income <50%, AQR c.25bps, RoTE >16%. It implies attributable profit of about GBP 5.8bn and RoTE of about 17% on GBP 33bn TNAV. Margins hold for two years as hedge income compounds, then fade to 35% (PBT margin about 37.5%) as impairment normalises to about 30bps through the cycle and deposit competition erodes the hedge spread. Terminal RoTE is about 15%, a 5pt spread over the 10% CoE. Management's 2028 >18% / 2030 c.20% RoTE guidance is deliberately NOT adopted in the base; it is the bull path.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 1.521 x g/(1+g), which holds CET1 at the 13.0% target as RWA grows with income.
base.tax_rationale: UK 25% plus 3% bank surcharge. H1-26 ETR on PBT after AT1 coupons was 28.8%; the TTM 30.2% is inflated by the partly non-deductible motor provision. Held at 28.5%.

bull.margin_rationale: Management's 2027-30 plan lands: the structural hedge locks in higher yields for longer, the strategic-initiative revenues (Lloyds Wealth via Schroders Personal Wealth, Lex/Tusker, Commercial capital-lite, high-single-digit OOI CAGR) arrive, and cost:income moves below 45% by 2030. Motor-finance redress settles within the existing GBP 1.95bn provision. Terminal RoTE is about 18-19%, close to the 2028 >18% guidance.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%, and bull cut from 35% to 30%, matching the LYG weighting of the same equity. Lloyds is a pure UK-domestic lender, so its whole book is exposed to one economy and one rate cycle. The motor-finance redress outcome is unresolved (FCA scheme partially suspended; Upper Tribunal hearing Dec 2026 or Feb 2027), and the shares already price in strong delivery (about 1.8x reported TNAV, versus about 1.1x for BCS). The bear is still lighter than BCS/HSBA.L's 25%: Lloyds has no investment-bank or EM exposure, a mortgage-heavy book, and guidance has been raised rather than cut.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
